title: Reverse: why save first?
prompt: In the reverse loop, why must `ListNode next = curr.next;` come BEFORE `curr.next = prev;`?
options: Flipping the pointer destroys the only path to the rest of the list — save it or lose it
explanation: `curr.next = prev` overwrites the forward link. Without the saved reference, the unvisited remainder of the list becomes unreachable.

title: Drill: middle node
prompt: From memory: return the middle node of the list using fast & slow pointers (for even lengths, the second middle — which is what this template naturally gives). The grader compares the list from the node you return.

solution.explanation: Fast moves twice as far, so when it exhausts the list, slow is halfway. The `fast != null && fast.next != null` guard order is load-bearing.

hints: If one walker moves twice as fast as another, where is the slow one when the fast one finishes?
Start both at head; move slow one step and fast two steps per iteration.
`while (fast != null && fast.next != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next; }`

title: Drill: remove all nodes with a value (dummy head)
prompt: From memory (dummy head): remove every node equal to `val` and return the head. The dummy node kills the special case of deleting the first node.

solution.explanation: With a dummy in front, every node — including the original head — has a predecessor, so one splice rule covers all cases. Not advancing after a splice handles runs like `7,7,7`. O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: Removing the head is a special case... unless the head also has a node in front of it.
Put a dummy node before head and look one node ahead: decide about `cur.next`, not `cur`.
Match → `cur.next = cur.next.next;` (stay put, the new next may match too); else `cur = cur.next;`. Return `dummy.next`.

title: Template recall: reverse a list
explanation: Save the forward link before flipping it, point the current node back at `prev`, then advance both pointers. When `curr` falls off the end, `prev` is the old tail — the new head. O(n) time, O(1) space.

title: Drill: k-th node from the end
prompt: From memory (a gap of k): return the k-th node from the END of the list (`k = 1` is the last node; `1 ≤ k ≤ length`), in one pass. The grader compares the list from the node you return.

solution.explanation: After fast moves k steps, slow and fast are k nodes apart; moving them together keeps the gap, so when fast falls off the end (null), slow is exactly k nodes from it. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.

hints: Two pointers a fixed distance apart stay that distance apart as they move together.
Advance one pointer k steps first, then move both until the leader runs off the end.
`for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) fast = fast.next;` then `while (fast != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next; }`.
